adds.title: Diputados aprueban reforma en beneficio de la comunidad trans (La Jornada Zacatecas)
adds.summary: La Jornada Zacatecas, 23 December 2022, reports that with 14 votes in favour and 7 against, deputies of the state's 64th Legislature approved the reform of the Family Code of the State of Zacatecas on gender identity, establishing the possibility of issuing a new birth certificate recognising an applicant's gender identity, principally for the trans community; the Justice Committee had already issued a positive opinion (dictamen) on the reform. This is the local record of the 2022 enactment against which this record's central claim — that Zacatecas is not among the states lacking a legislated gender-recognition procedure — is checked. Page verified via the Wayback Machine snapshot of 7 October 2025; the live ljz.mx URL is Cloudflare-blocked (HTTP 403).

adds.title: ¡Eso! Zacatecas prohíbe las terapias de conversión o los ECOSIG (Sopitas)
adds.summary: Sopitas, 30 August 2021, reports that on 25 August 2021 the Congress of Zacatecas approved prohibiting and sanctioning conversion therapies or 'ECOSIG' (Esfuerzos para Corregir la Orientación Sexual e Identidad de Género) by adding fraction VI to article 182 Bis of the state Penal Code — penalised with one to three years' imprisonment or up to 300 days of community work against anyone who incites hatred or violence on grounds of sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or promotes such practices; the same session also typified hate crimes motivated by sexual orientation and gender identity in the state Penal Code. The article further records that the gender-identity law initiative debated alongside (constitutional and family-code reform) failed to obtain enough votes and remained pending at the time — the reform only passed in December 2022. Documents the protective state-level criminal-law floor applying in Zacatecas, with an explicit ban on practices aimed at changing gender identity.

adds.title: Gender Recognition in Mexico by State (Human Rights Watch)
adds.summary: Human Rights Watch's March 2025 state-by-state feature on legal gender recognition carries a dedicated Zacatecas entry: in 2022 the state congress passed a reform amending the Family Code to create an administrative procedure for legal gender recognition, and in 2023 the director of the state Civil Registry issued guidelines implementing the law, both linked to the official state gazette (periodico.zacatecas.gob.mx). This is the per-state framework source consistent with the record's statement that, in HRW's March 2025 count (22 of 32 states having legislated a procedure at the time), Zacatecas is not among the states lacking one.

adds.title: Changes to Vital Statistics Act Would Allow for Change of Sex Designation (Government of Newfoundland and Labrador news release)
adds.summary: Government of Newfoundland and Labrador news release, 17 June 2021: proposed changes to the Vital Statistics Act, 2009 would allow residents of the province who were not born there — but have lived there at least three months — to change their sex designation; the change certificate carries a $25 fee, counts as official provincial identification and 'could be leveraged by the applicant to update records in other jurisdictions,' serving as the identification document for people born outside the country. The release states the amendments align with earlier changes allowing a non-binary option on provincial birth certificates; the bill received second reading that day and Royal Assent on 23 June 2021. Gives the province a resident-based legal gender-change route (three-month residency) relevant to document enrolment for trans people in Newfoundland and Labrador.

adds.title: Legislative Amendment Respects Rights of Transgender Individuals (Government of Newfoundland and Labrador news release)
adds.summary: Government of Newfoundland and Labrador news release, 12 April 2016: an amendment to the Vital Statistics Act, 2009 removes the requirement to undergo sex-reassignment surgery before changing the gender marker on a birth or marriage registration, bringing provincial law into compliance with an order of a Board of Inquiry under the provincial Human Rights Commission (the December 2015 ruling on complaints from two trans women) and with LGBTQ advocates' requests. The province's gender-marker change on provincial records has therefore operated without a surgery requirement since the 2016 amendment (Royal Assent 13 April 2016).

adds.title: Changing Your Sex Designation (Government of Newfoundland and Labrador)
adds.summary: Current official Government of Newfoundland and Labrador page: applicants for a change of sex designation must be 16 or older, or be represented by a parent or legal guardian for under-16s (with consent of the other parent/guardian and written consent of individuals aged 12 to 15), and must be born in the province or have resided there at least three months; there is no fee for the change application, with charges applying only to official copies of updated documents (new birth certificate $35, or $30 online). The province states it cannot guarantee that a birth certificate with an 'X' gender marker will be accepted by authorities in other organisations — the documented cross-border document caveat relevant to carrying provincial records elsewhere.

adds.title: P.E.I. transgender community applauds ID changes (CBC News)
adds.summary: CBC News, 18 April 2016, reports that the MacLauchlan government tabled a bill to amend the Vital Statistics Act so Islanders can change their gender on official documents by declaring the gender they identify with plus a letter from a doctor, with sex-reassignment surgery no longer required; Pride P.E.I. board member Jesse Macmillan welcomed the move, noting surgery is expensive and the closest provider was in Montreal, and called for a future third gender category, adding that many of his friends in Charlottetown identify outside the binary; a linked item on the article page reports Health PEI would cover the costs of three surgeries for transgender patients. PEI's gender-marker change on provincial documents has worked without a surgery requirement since the 2016 amendment.

adds.title: Improving diversity and inclusion on driver's licences (Government of Prince Edward Island news release)
adds.summary: Government of Prince Edward Island news release, 30 November 2018: Islanders may now select 'gender not listed' (shown on the licence as X) or 'prefer not to say' (blank) alongside male and female when identifying gender on a driver's licence; the release states PEI is the first jurisdiction in Canada to offer the 'prefer not to say'/blank option, quoting Transportation, Infrastructure and Energy Minister Paula Biggar and PEERS Alliance. The change took effect 4 December 2018 at Access PEI locations, meaning provincial photo ID can carry an X or blank gender marker.

adds.title: Change of Gender Designation (Government of Prince Edward Island)
adds.summary: Official Government of PEI information page (content as captured in the Wayback Machine snapshot of 1 July 2022; the live page is bot-gated): an adult may apply for a change of gender designation if born in PEI and resident in the province for at least three months and not in the lawful custody of another person; a legal custodian may apply for a minor under 18 who was born on PEI and has lived in the province at least three months, with written consent of any other custodian or parent and of the child if aged 12 or older. The application requires completed forms including a physician statement, a written statement by the applicant, and signature arranged before a commissioner of oaths at Vital Statistics — a provincial gender-marker regime operating without a surgery requirement and with physician attestation.
